B: 390 Optical Wedge

ProbDesc: Request CAL LAB to provide calibration support for spot welder force gauge. LPS 412 B Qualification and Certification of Resistance Welding requires that a force gauge be used to ensure the machine is regularly calibrated. The user would simply be the artisan that is operating the resistance welder, they don’t need any certification to use the gauge as it is a minor but necessary part of using the resistance welder, and a simple instruction of how to check the force would be a part of any training they receive for resistance welding qualification. The machine accuracy is +/- 3% and the digital force gauge we will need Cal Lab support for has an accuracy of 0.5%. The excerpt of the LPS 412B that speaks to the force gauge is as follows: An electrode tip force gauge, which has been calibrated and meets or exceeds the force rating of the machine, shall be used every month, and prior to qualification of a machine or certification of a schedule, to verify the accuracy of the indicated tip or electrode force reading of the machine. The accuracy of the gauge shall meet or exceed that of the machine it is being used on and calibration shall be performed annually. https://www.tuffaloy.com/products/accessories/weld-force-gauges/601-5000dlc-digital-weld-gauge-5000lb-2272kg-22-24kn-with-case

TEInst:
Metrology Engineering at FRCSW will reauthorize SDB to calibrate TI 87501436-101 (CAGE Code: 81873) with the

following guidance:

The STS stand has a requirement in the ICP 17-20MX-226 to be calibrated to a max torque range of 45k in-lbs,

this is achieved by applying a max of 15k in-lbs of torque with the STD, which is multiplied by a gear ratio of 3 to

achieve the required 45k in-lbs.

The STD does not have an ICP and could be calibrated with the ICP 17-20MU-55 that calibrates the cousin C/D STS

torque standard although that ICP maxes out at 10k in-lbs, does not have the appropriate moment arms and weights

needed to reach the max range of 20k in-lbs.

The ICP does include the proper methodology so the proposed solution is to use the ICP 17-20MU-55 to calibrate

using the following STDs from ICP 17-20MU-52: Calibration Lever TSD6552-1 (61015) and additional Weights

TSD2085 (61015) and other ancillary equipment as needed.

Please calibrate with the attached checklist (TEI00154644-1720MU5X) with an interval of 12 months

________________

Recommend Submitting CPR against the ICP 17-20MU-56 for the issues related to the smaller range torque cell:

1. The Torque Transducer required for the LEF TORQUE CALIBRATION KIT, has a stated range of 1000 In-lbs in

METRL; however, the ICP that is recommended by METRL to calibrate it has a limit of 800 in-lbs according to Table

1. Table 2 states the effective range of the standards is 1000 in-lbs. Recommend updating table 1 to reflect the range

of the standards.

2. The workload ICP 17-20MX- 226 states a minimum use specification to reach a range of 1,100 in-lbs. If the

METRL Range is correct then the STD is not capable of meeting the Minimum Use Specification which is required in

step 4.3.2 of the ICP. There is no mention of a torque gear ratio to compensate for the lack or range.

Recommend submitting CPR against the ICP 17-20MX-226 for issues regarding Table 1 and Table 2.

1. In Table 1, the Performance Specifications of 49,000 in-lbs should be updated to 45,000 in-lbs as that is the

highest point that is tested.

2. In Table 2, the minimum use specifications should be updated for item 2.9.2 and item 2.9.3. It should be updated to

read 45,000 in-lbs and Range ±75°, respectively.

Note 1: In ICP 17-20MX-226, the calibration equipment used to verify the 1100 in-lb requirement does not meet a 4:1

TAR.

Note 2: This interim guidance will be provided to prevent work-stoppage. LCP (and other related documents such as

the CRA, MUA) will be developed and completed tentatively before the next calibration due date.

TEInst:
Metrology Engineering at FRCSW has determined the probe of the 5 AXIS MACHINE part no. DMC 125FD should be user verified on a regular basis using calibrated artifacts.



As discussed in the email attachment, the features being milled on the 5 AXIS MACHINE will be checked for final accuracy using calibrated micrometers or CMM after work on the mill is completed. However, It is on the understanding that the long term vision for the 5 AXIS MACHINE is to have full milling and measurement capability without the usage of external micrometer measurement. In order to achieve this, Metrology Engineer recommends the usage of a user verification procedure in order to build a log of data and statistical process control (SPC) on probe accuracy for later analysis and build the confident in using the machine for manufacturing and verification of parts.



NOTES AND RECOMMENDATIONS:



The calibration kit that was purchased along with the 5 axis machines to contain parts that are insufficient for verifying the accuracy of the touch probe of the mill.



1.There are significant concerns about the way the gage block is being used in current user verification procedures, changes to this procedure are highly recommended. Please contact Metrology Engineering for the recommendation on the procedure deviation from OEM manual for the user verification section. With this modified user verification methodology, metrology engineering recommends for two additional  gage blocks with different sizes and meets the standards of ASME AS-2 grade based on its size to be added to the current kit. The gage blocks will be sent to SDB for calibration.



2.The master sphere that was included in the kit is not supported for calibration by SDB at the moment but based on current requirement, the sphere isn't being utilized. If in the future, calibration of the master spheres become necessary due to new requirements, please submit another REQ for new calibration procedure to be developed for those master sphere.



3.The dial indicator within the calibration kits need to be sent to SDB for calibration. It is appropriate for use during user verification if calibration data can be confirmed to be within a tolerance of ±100 µin.



4.The current ring gage is not accurate enough to calibrate the probe to a suitable degree of accuracy. The artifact being used to calibrate the probe for bore measurements should be accurate to ±0.0001 in in order to verify probe accuracy for a part needed at the tightest a tolerance of ±0.0004 in. The current artifact ring gage does not meet this standard. Therefore, Metrology recommends two class X ring gage from 0.5-4.5 inches in diameter be added in replacement of the ring gage in the current calibration kit during user verification.

TEInst:
From review of provided calibration data from 17-51MD-014, the Collins Microflat 48 x 144 inch granite surface plate meets Grade AA tolerance of 975 µin for overall flatness, and Grade AA tolerance of 100 µin for localized surface deviations (repeatability).  Grade tolerances taken from ASME B89.3.7 for a granite surface plate of diagonal 151 inches in length.

Use worksheet data to create surface deviation topographic map from all 8 lines.  Create topographic map for repeatability data as well.

The 48 x 144 inch granite surface plate may be used for flatness measurements anywhere on its surface to an accuracy of 550 µin.  For tests requiring flatness accuracy greater than 550 µin., use topographic map to identify areas that meet accuracy requirement.
  
Any spot on the surface plate will provide repeat readings to within 40 µin.  The topographic map of repeatometer readings may be used to identify spots with repeatability better than 40 µin.

For future calibrations using the autocollimator method of 17-51MD-014, the Moody method requires that center line tie-in tolerances be within 100 µin.

From "How to Calibrate Surface Plates in the Plant" by J.C. Moody:

"The center line check is the criterion of accuracy for the entire operation.  The value at the point at which the center lines and diagonals intersect is physically zero.  If everything were done perfectly, the value opposite the center station would be zero.  But this is not possible because each slight error in reading the instrument is reflected at the mid station of the center lines.  If the magnitude of this error is under 0.0001, the calibration may be regarded as satisfactory; if not, the job must be done over."
WorkNotes: Review of provided worksheets shows that max deviation from mean base plane was 542 µin, meeting the tolerance of 975, and max local surface deviation of 40 µin, meeting a tolerance of 100 µin for Grade AA as defined in ASME B89.3.7.  Line tie-in tolerances did not meet 100 µin. As directed by J.C. Moody.  Will provide guidance for future calibrations using the moody method.
StatusTicket: Data looks good enough to classify as Grade AA.  Can use topographic maps to identify flat and repeatable areas.

TEInst:
Metrology Engineering at FRCSW authorizes SDB or higher capability lab to calibrate the ATOS SCANBOX, Model#: ATOS 6130 (CAGE: CJ908) as follows:



Procedure: User calibration before use and at the end of the day. Use Manufacture Calibration Procedure. (See Notes 1, 2, and 3)

Range: 0.000 millimeter to 1300.000 millimeter (See note 4)

Tolerance: +/-(336 + 116.8 * L) micrometer for L meters (See note 5)

Interval: User calibration before use and at the end of the day



Please submit a REQ for the Calibrate Panel, model CP40/MV1000 (Cage CJ908), so interim calibration guidance can be provided. Recommend procuring scale bars, high resolution camera, and photogrametric software.



Note 1: Model# CP40/MV1000 (CAGE code: CJ908) Calibration Panel is the standard used to calibrate the ATOS 6130. Currently, NPSL and SDB do not have the capability to calibrate the Calibration Panel. It would be difficult to get the OEM (GOM) on a COMSP approved list, since they are a foreign entity. Dynamic Corporation, a U.S. based company, has the scope and competency to calibrate the Calibration Panel with NIST traceable standards. As an interim due to COVID-19, a waiver can be provided for a COMSP approval for Dynamic Corporation to calibrate the Calibration Panel Model# CP40/MV1000. The Calibration Panel is a new technology and different than all previous technology, so a generic interval of 12 months is suitable for this item.



Note 2: Qplus Labs, a U.S. based lab, uses Coordinate Measuring Machine (CMM) as a standard in their calibration methodology, but current NAVAIR policy does not authorize it as standard.



Note 3: Please acquire another Calibration Panel, Model# CP40/MV1000 (CAGE code: CJ908) with NIST Traceable certificate to be used as a reference standard, along with a protective transit case. The existing Calibration Panel will be used as a working standard, since it is being mounted on the SCANBOX wall where the ATOS resides.



Note 4: The calibration panel diagonal measurement is the largest dimension, 1300.000 millimeter.



Note 5: Consult Metrology Engineering when tolerance tighter than +/-(336 + 116.8 * L) micrometer for L meters is required. Tolerance of +/-(336 + 116.8 * L) micrometer for L meters is derived by working down from the Standard Scale Bar to the Calibration Panel, then to the ATOS 6130.



a. Standard Scale Bar tolerance: +/-(21 + 7.3 * L)). Standard Scale Bar used by Dynamic Corporation to calibrate the Calibration Panel.

b. Calibration Panel tolerance: 4 * Standard Scale Bar tolerance = +/-(84 + 29.3 * L)). Calibration Panel used by ATOS 6130 to calibrate system.

c. ATOS 6130 tolerance: 4 * Calibration Panel tolerance = +/-(336 + 116.8 * L)). ATOS 6130 used to inspect parts and make intolerance or out of tolerance decision.

Engineering drawing uses 0.0005 in. tolerance.  This is a LIS that uses a method that adds length values based on pin diameter to measurement values.  The pin dimensions are not traceable in the LIS to anything.

Decimal number from LIS represents the distance from the bottom of the supporting construction ball or pin to the contact point where the master gauge is supported.  The master gauges are machined with a 35° or 45° support slope at their top end.  The vertical distance component for the contact point of the master gauge can be found by taking the sine of the slope angle.  The resulting "X" dimension is found by multiplying the support ball or pin radius by (1+ sine component).

ProbDesc:
A CPR has been submitted for NAVAIR 17-20MD- 06 stating the following:

    The NOTES after step 4.1 state “TI’s used in precision work or any TI with re-lapped anvil or spindle faces require flatness tests. If the user requirements are known to be general purpose, (toolbox issue, used to measure diameter dimensions where flatness is not a factor, accuracy of measurement is not critical, etc.) a flatness test is not required. Affix a SPECIAL CALIBRATION label to the TI stating “Flatness not tested” and proceed to step 4.2.”

     Does the first note after 4.2 apply to TI’s where flatness was not tested, because the second paragraph in that note states flatness is required? If it is required, then there should be additional guidance to proceed to step 4.3.

    If both sections 4.1 and 4.2 are skipped shouldn’t the TI’s SPECIAL CALIBRATION state “Flatness and parallelism not tested”?

Request guidance until CPR is answered.


CPR No.: SDB211262 (CPR Log No.: 2021-2279 / CPR Activity Tracking No.: SDBM06)
TEInst:
Upon discussion with dimensional SME of NSWC Corona, the following is what was discussed.

1)  The first paragraph of the NOTE following Section 4.1 should be omitted or revised completely.  SME states that if the measuring face is flat, then flatness will need to be tested (regardless of user requirements).
2)  Parallelism can only be tested if both measuring faces are flat and if the measuring range does not exceed 1 inch (which is noted in step 4.2.1).
3)  If parallelism is not tested, then a conditional statement needs to be added to the NOTE following Section 4.2 to skip to Section 4.3.
4)  SPECIAL CAL label may not be necessary as SPECIAL CAL implies that the TI is modified, whether it be the tolerance, measuring range, etc.  Since some micrometers are built without a flat measuring face, then certain Sections of the ICP are simply not applicable.

It is agreed between Metrology Engineering and the dimensional SME that the NOTES need to be revised with the proper conditional statements.

NOTE:  The points made above will be submitted to NSWC Corona as part of the evaluation for the CPR.  However, there is no guarantee that the ICP will be changed in accordance with the points listed here.

This is a one time authorization that is valid for 120 days.
WorkNotes:
The purpose of this REQ was to make a substitution of a granite surface plate that is called out in the ICP with a larger surface plate that the technicians had on hand. The surface plate is used as a standard to calibrate the TI which is a Propeller Protractor. The technicians submit an REQ because there is a process that is used to validate new procedures which might affect the actual accuracy of the part.
By looking at the State of the Problem, CAGE code and the model numbers of the standards are given. The TI cage code is not given, that can be looked up on the Measure website by looking up the model number. Look for a CAGE code from a number that ends in R. Shop Support only works with R-coded assets. 
Look up and read over the procedure that is referenced in the REQ. Most of the answers for this REQ can be inferred from reading the ICP and talking to technicians. From the first page of the ICP, listed below the titles are three currently supported protractors. One them that can found in METPRO is the Warren Knight 23-1990. One important aspect of the ICP to be wary of is the publication on the bottom right corner. Anything that is old will have its credibility put into question.
Table 1 of the procedure includes the information about the TI including its characteristics, the range and tolerance, and the method. Looking at is from right to left, is can be seen that the Test Method for both TI characteristics does not include the mention of a surface plate, only a sine plate and TI angle. Under performance specifications, we see the range intervals of 30, 45, and 60. For this TI, degrees between the three numbers are not taken as anything besides that is not considered. 
Table 2 is the next significant table section to look at as it provides the standards that are being used and what their specifications are. One thing to notice is that under minimum use specifications for the surface plate, it gives use the size and class. That can be used to find a reference in the ASME standards handbook for surface plates, this part is older so it will be under support a book that is no longer used. Another significant thing to notice is that there is no mention of flatness in the specification, which is odd since that is an important aspect of flatness.
Section 4 which is the calibration process is also significant because it details how the technicians use the surface plate. The angle indication test shows the surface plate is used to level the plate. Looking through the rest of the procedure, the surface plate is used to clamp the sine plate down. But thinking at this from the sine plate point of view, there is no need for surface plate as it does not play a significant role in the angle of the sine plate. The sine plate itself has an adjustable level that allows it to zero.
StatusTicket: Nearing completion. Currently need to fill out database with response. Reviewed ICP calibration process to determine that surface plate Substitution has no significant, quantifiable effect on Propeller Protractor Procedure. Substitution is allowed.

WorkNotes:
Purpose of this REQ was for a substitution of a Supafina (Taft Pierce) Sine plate in for a Brown and Sharpe Sine Plate for the ICP of a propeller protractor. The significance of the sine plate in the ICP is for the angle creation in testing the angle readings of the protractor. The propeller protractor is used as an angle measuring device, part of the calibration involved with testing it is to measure various angles at 30, 45, 60 and 90 degrees. The Supafina Sine Plate is a compound roller Laboratory Grade sine plate that uses angle blocks to create a height at one end to generate angle.

TI Tolerance was calculated using directions in Notes section under TI Tolerance Table under 17-20MD-30 in Matlab for 30, 45, and 60 degrees. Angle of 90 degrees can be ignored since it is not used in the generation of angle for Propeller Protractor. Plugging these tolerances into MUA yields PFA under 2%.

After emailing manufacturer, it is confirmed that at 30 degrees, 9229 Sine Plate has angle tolerance of 15 arc seconds. Manufacturer was not able to confirm an other angles, 17-20MD-30 was used as the basis for angle tolerance calculation.

TitleTicket: AKI and AKF request to add FS55-10K,PLATFORM SCALE to the CPAR
WorkNotes:
The purpose of this REQ is to address AKI and AKF’s request to add Indiana Scale Platforms Scale to CPAR. Lab suggested the use of LCP-AKI-MM-001. The Platform scale has a maximum measurement of 10,000 lbs and a resolution of 2lbs with divisions of 5000. Manufacturer was not able to provide specifications regarding the tolerance of the platform scale. Table 6. From Pg73 of the NIST Handbook 44 -2022 can be applied to find the tolerance. Definition of resolution is equivalent to scale division terminology in NIST. From given pictures and model number of platform, it is known that the Platform Scale has a class of III. Applying Table 6., tolerance is 2lb for first 1000lb measured, and doubles in the next increment measurement of 1000lb-4000lb to be a tolerance of 4lb. Tolerance of 6lb between 4000 and 8000 lb. 
Tolerances of Platform Scale were not given, Table 6 of page 74 NIST Handbook 44, 2022 Edition was applied. Tolerances of Table 6 was given in scale divisions with 2 be the scale division (resolution). 
Uncertainty of weights was found to be ±650mg for class C 50 lb weight and ±2.3 g for Class F 50 lb according to ICP 17-20MM-04. Quantitative limits on the number of weights that AKI and AKF have are 94 of 50LB Class "C" weights and 46 of 50LB Class "F" weights, total 7,000LB(4,700LB + 2,300LB) as STD Weights. Uncertainties were added together according to their respective weights and combinations, uncertainty results are listed in table to the right.
Through email with Toshio, it is confirmed that user requirements for the device will be a max weight measurement of 7000 lb. It has also been confirmed though email with Toshio that AKI and AFK have standards in the form of Class C and F weights that total a max weight of 7000 lb. This is fortunate for this situation because CPAR managers require the use of standards weights for the calibration procedure. If shop did not have enough standard weights then, the use of dead weights as given in the LCP, would not pass CPAR submission. A note of a “Special Calibration Label” will need to be stuck on to the device to know that it is rated only up to 7000 lb.
Instead of LCP-AKI-MM-001, General Calibration Guidance 17-20MM-01 will be used for CPAR submission due to it having a better odd of getting into CPAR. The requirement for using this ICP is that it falls within the range of 20,000 lb and that its tolerance is 0.1% of the initial value or greater. ProbDesc: Request authorization to immediately apply ICP 17-20AZ-145 instruction addition recommendations concurrently submitted via CPR #34664 (SDB-AZ145), as detailed below: ICP 17-20AZ-145 is missing critical set-up instructions that ARE already included in its earlier predecessor ICP, 17-20AZ-71. This missing guidance can and has led to erroneous out-of-tolerance measurements and falsely rejected items. Recommend borrowing from 17-20AZ-71 and inserting the following four instruction additions to clarify set-ups and improve measurement repeatability in 17-20AZ-145: 1) Step 4.1.1: Expand step wording (similar to 17-20AZ-71 step 4.1.1) to read “Set the universal counter (item 2.1) for a frequency measurement of 1 kHz on channel 1. Press the channel X10 attenuator and 100 KHz Low Pass Filter pushbuttons to turn these functions ON.” 2) Step 4.1.3: Add an additional sentence to this step (similar to 17-20AZ-71 step 4.1.3) to read “Ensure both prongs on each TI Kelvin clip make electrical contact.” 3) Step 4.2.1: After the first sentence, add an additional sentence to this step (similar to 17-20AZ-71 step 4.2.3 Table-bottom Notes 2 & 3) to read “Remove shorting bar between the decade low and guard terminals.” 4) Step 4.2.3: Expand or add an additional sentence to this step (similar to 17-20AZ-71 step 4.2.3 Table-bottom Notes 2 & 3) to read “Connect guard terminal to the TI rear-panel –BIAS terminal.” * NOTE: Alternate ICP, 17-20AZ-119, would also benefit from the same corrections listed above as its step instructions are nearly identical in their omissions.
TEInst:
Metrology Engineering at FRCSW authorizes the changes in procedures for 17-20AZ-145 as follows:

1) Step 4.1.1: Set the universal counter for a frequency measurement of 1kHz on channel 1.  Press the channel 1 X10 attenuator and 100 KHz Low Pass Filter pushbuttons to turn these functions ON.

2) Step 4.1.3: Connect the TI Kelvin clips to the universal counter input using the BNC to binding post adapter.  Ensure that both prongs on each Kelvin clip make electrical contact. Observe correct polarity.

3) Step 4.2.1: Use the digital multimeter to measure the 1 and 10 Ohm setting of decade resistor 1 in 4-wire mode.  Remove shorting bar between the decade low and guard terminals.  Note the two resistance readings for use in later steps.  Disconnect the decade resistor 1 from the digital multimeter.

4) Step 4.2.3:  Connect the TI Kelvin Clips to the decade resistor 1.  Connect guard terminal to the TI rear-panel - BIAS terminal.

Attached previous Final Report and Guidance of  TEI-00161870 plus LCP-AKI-MM-001. MN C3B1-5T-NS is the load cell and MN CSD-903-EX is the indicator.
TEInst:
Metrology Engineering at FRCSW authorizes AKI to calibrate TI model: C3B1-5T-NS and CSD-903-EX [S0352] PALLET SCALES (Load Cell and Load Cell Indicator) as follows:



Procedure: LCP-AKI-MM-001

Range: 11,000 lbs as per Customer's Requirements. Total range of TI is 15,000 lbs.

Tolerance: +/-0.5% of FS (as a Demand Accuracy)

Interval: 12 months



NOTE: Affix a black-on-yellow SPECIAL CALIBRATION label to the TI indicating the “TI is tested up to 11,000lbs.”
TitleTicket: AKI requests re-authorization to calibrate TI, MN C3B1-5T-NS/CSD-903-EX, Pallet Scale.
WorkNotes:
This REQ is similar to my previous REQs of REQ-00184562 and REQ-00184563 as they are scales and use the same LCP as those. Also referencing REQ-00161870 has this was previously authorized. From surface level, authorization will be approved as this specific LCP is not able to get into CPAR and these scales using this LCP will stay in the REQ world.

MUA is performed. From my understanding, the TI would be the load cell and the standards would be the standard weights and the load cell indicator. This Load cell and the indicator is part of a bigger system with Model No. F16-0813. An email was sent to originator to verify tolerance of TI and if it still holds that only up to 11,000 LBs is being calibrated (special cal).

An email was received to confirm tolerance and range from the originator. The range is 11,000 lbs with a tolerance of 0.5% FS. Upon research, the accuracy comes from a "Inspection Data" sheet. The accuracy is for the pallet scale with model no. F16-0183. That pallet scale includes the load cell and load cell indicator, which means that the tolerance of the pallet scale is everything combined.

Only problem I have currently having is how to account for the unknown uncertainty of the steel pallets (which are not standard weights) to achieve the higher test points. After discussion with SME, the substituion method which is being used in the LCP confirms the weight that the standards alone are calibrating to, in this case 7000 lbs. To calibrate the last 4,000 lbs to create 11,000 lbs, steel pallets were added, but steel pallets were added to create 7,000 since that point became calibrated, so the uncertainty should be the standard times 2.

TEInst:

WorkNotes:
The purpose of this REQ-00185814 is for the reauthorization of TEI-00101670 that is used to calibrate 847 Backflow Test Kit Pressure Gage. Since this is a reauthorization, there is some documentation that can be found within the database regarding useful information such as what type of pressure gage, the standards used, and GCG was recommended.
Searching the NPSL database with the TEI yields a folder which includes the emails, TI data sheets, CPAR requests and checklists. One thing to note is that there seems to have been a mistake regarding the recommended use of MP-04 which should have been corrected to MP-41. For the purposes of following previous checklist notation, MP-06 will be used, but MP-41 could also be used.
Searching in the PSM database yields the MUA of other interchangeable standards that were used. For the MUA calculation of the 847, four standards will be taken into account. Running MUA analysis results in all passing with under 2%.
Test points are 90%, 70%, 50%, and 25% of full scale.  Since 25% of 15 psid is 3.75 and the face of the gage does not have minor tick marks, the lowest test point was changed to 3.5psid for easier verification. PSID is used for differential pressure as a measure of the difference of two pressures.

TEInst:
Metrology Engineering at FRCSW authorizes SDB lab to calibrate TI Model MK36EWRRD (Cage Code: 28591) Ultrasonic Cleaner, Serial Number JB2796-17 for temperature using CALSTD Thermocouple Simulator Calibrator 1140A, along with the following guidance:

Procedure: 17-20ST-78
Range: 120°F -  160°F
Tolerance: ±20 °F
Interval: 12 Months

Note 1: Authorization is only for drying portion of Ultra Sonic Cleaner over specified temperature range.

Note 2: Previous REQs 00163471 and 00174780 will use procedure 17-20ST-236 with range and tolerance of 120 ± 15 °F for Stage One-Ultrasonic Wash, Stage Two-Overflowing Rinse, and Stage Three-Counterflowing Rinse which is different process than this REQ. This REQ is only for Stage Four-Heated Dryer. For calibration of entire TI, both procedures 17-20ST-226 and 17-20ST-78 will need to be used.
WorkNotes:
The purpose of this procedure is to get guidance on the calibration of the fourth bin of the ultrasonic cleaner which is the dry heat process. There have been previously REQs that aim to address this for the previous three bins in the ultrasonic cleaning process. The reason that SDB is sending this request is that there was a period of time where the REQ was sent and the start of calibration, when the start of calibration commenced, it was found that the upper range of 140 Fahrenheit was not enough for drying. To solve this, SDB recommended 17-20ST-78.

The initial REQ 00163471 was initially sent in to get calibration of MK36EWRRD with a range of 100-190. But it can also be seen in the “Overflowing Rinse” picture in the first REQ folder that the Solution Temp is 100-140F. 

Regarding the first REQ, in an email with RAMCO, it was stated that for an ultrasonic cleaner, calibration can be done on the sonic fuse holders which have about 6-7 amps. It is at round this current that there are bubbles that are formed at temps of 120-140F. Another piece that might need calibration is the Digital Temperature Gauges, but RAMCO has assured that they usually only need to be checked with a dial thermometer or digital hand held to check that range is ± 3 degrees. It was also stated in the email that there is a manual that listed 200F as the max temp the controller can be set to, above that would cause it boil (boil temp of water = 212F). Other possibilities of calibration is 20-25 psi. There is also height of stroke where the platform moves up and down. It is also confirmed that the perfect operating temperature is 120-140F ±3F. This tolerance of ±3F is probably was used as the TI’s tolerance of the MUA tolerance. Another important piece of information is the Counter flowing rinse operating instruction that is found on the Tank CS-3 where it is stated that the solution temperature is 100-140F. This 100F is probably was used as the lowest number in the TI’s range.

There is another piece of documentation provided from William Castillo Latorre where he provided a LPS from the FRCSW Technical Library stating that a “heated air dryer tank shall produce dry heated air between 120°F - 160°F with a relative humidity below 10%. This range will be used for the drying bin range in the MUA calculation. This LPS seems to be a general procedure on how to clean parts in a supersonic cleaner. In the Table 1 of the LPS, solution identification that is used is Daraclean 212 Aqueous Degreaser with a operating temperature of 80-180F and a recommended temperature of 140-150F. Time that is used to dry is as necessary. 

UUT used for MUA is the fourth bin of the RAMCO Ultra Sonic Cleaner which is used a dryer in the ultra-sonic cleaning process. ICP 17-20ST-78 will be used as it pertains to the use of dry ovens. It was confirmed with William E Castillo Latorre though LPS-NI-MATL-0113 in paragraph 5.1.4 that the recommended drying temperature is 120°F-160°F. A mean value of 140°F was used as the measurement point. One measurement point will be used according to section 4.2 and for ease of measurement. Section 4.2 will be used because Section 3.4 indicates using step 4.2 for standard Ectron 1140A Thermocouple simulator/calibrator.

A UUT Tolerance of ±20°F to fall within the recommended range of 120°F-160°F, but is not too big to encroach the range boundary. A value of 20 was also used to follow consistencies with other previous guidance for Ultra Sonic Cleaning bins. In the Measurement Uncertainty 4% was used according to Table 2 with a Normal Distribution of k=2.

Uncertainties for standards was found using Table 2 of 17-20ST-78 with ±0.112°F for Type K and ±0.837 °F for the Type R or S. Applying this yields PFA under 2% and TUR above 4. 12 month interval will be used following previous REQs.

This is a note that this authorization is only for the 4th well as written in the interim guidance.

TitleTicket: AKI and AKF request to re-add MN 2001A to monthly CPAR DB#18608
WorkNotes:
The purpose of this REQ is that AKI and AKF is requesting CPAR submission of model 2001A which is similar to 2001 that was previously approved in CPAR. The only difference between 2001 and 2001A is the difference of a rubber cap for the leads. Doing further research, 2001 was approved in CPAR with a two procedures used. Model 2001 can also be found in METRL which uses 17-20AQ-348.

Going over the history of the model 2001A, the previous version was 2001 which also included 2001A. This connection can be seen in the description section of the current 2001 in CPAR Submission. This connection and the previous DB#17204 have been deleted due to database deletion caused by the nomenclature of “A” having a space and being unable to stay in METRL. The current 2001 in CPAR under DB#18608 was entered in 2013 when there was not a need for MUA and checklists. Part of this REQ and CPAR submission will also include an MUA and checklist to compensate for this.

MUA analysis for this REQ will include analysis for five criteria which included Alternating Current Voltage, Direct Current Voltage, Alternating Current, Direct Current, and Resistance. Looking at the history of the MEASURE card, Fluke 5080AAN is used as the calibrator, Fluke 5500A as the coil, and GenRad 1433 as the resistor. Manufacturer specification and ICP 17-50AX-038 was used for uncertainty of the 5080AAN. Manufacturer specification and ICP 17-20AQ-032 was used for Coil tolerances and resistance.

Tolerances for UUT were found using manufacturer specifications for the 2001A. For most of the TDME tolerances, they were found using specs and ICP.
Calculation were made for the current tolerances as the tolerances included both the current calibrator and 50-turn coil. The calibrator’s max current that can be outputted is 20 Amps, so for the first measurement point of 20A, the 50 turn coil’s tolerance can be ignored. For measurement points of 50 and 100, a coil will be used to increase the current. Uncertainty of the calibrator and coil was found from AQ-32 and the coil’s tolerance was inputted into the uncertainty tool.
In the calculations, there was an option to do RSS for total specification according to the Fluke 5500A/Coil instruction sheet, but that yielded a higher PFA. A special calibration interval will need to be used because AC and DC currents passes MUA for calibration interval of at least 8 months.

Maximum resistance of the resistor of the GenRad 1433W goes only up to 10MΩ but max range of 2001A multimeter is 34MΩ. Customer requirements require the max rated resistance of 34MΩ, to accomplish this, a second ICP will be used for the resistance measurements. ICP 17-20AQ-348 will be used as it has maximum resistance range of 2GΩ, but for our case we will only go up to 34MΩ. Resistance tolerances will be taken from 20AQ-32 and assumed to be used in combined in series to achieve more specific tolerances. To get the tolerances, RSS will be applied to the resistors at quantities of seven depending on what amount is needed. For example at 34kΩ, tolerances of three 10kΩ will be used and four 1kΩ. Doing this calculation for multiples of 34  yields a very low tolerance which can be seen in the resistance measurements. For simplicity, the highest tolerances at 34MΩ which is 0.008%, will be used for the MUA analysis to provide worst case scenario.

Calibration interval will need to be shortened from 12 months to 8 months to pass PFA. 

Two ICPs will be used to cover the full range TI characteristics.

The first REQ-00135147 gives authorization for SDB to use the TI 6240M46 but on the condition that ICP 17-50SV-009 be used. The reasoning for the use of a different procedure was due to them not having the required standard of Unholtz-Dickie 330B. This was done in June 12, 2020.

The second REQ-00135150 gives authorization for SDB to use the TI 6240M49 but on the condition that ICP 17-50SV-009 be used. The reasoning for the use of a different procedure was due to them not having the required standard of Unholtz-Dickie 330B. Unholtz-Dickie 8B6 Accelerometer and Unholtz-Dickie 680 Vibration Standard System are the authorized standards. This was given June 12, 2020.

The third REQ-00185693 which is also the latest REQ gives authorization for SDB to calibrate the Piezoelectric Accelerometers 6240M46  and 6240M49 using the shop recommended 17-20SV-06  with a different standard Unholtz Dickie 680 than what is called out. The 680 is the Vibration System Standard that is used in 17-50SV-009, the REQ does not call out Unholtz-Dickie 8B6 Lab Standard Accelerometer. This is alright since 8B6 part of the standard 680. 17-20SV-06 calls out for the use of Standard Unholtz-Dickie 330B instead.

Doing some research it was found the REQ was submitted back in May 2022, but it was only recently approved by Neal Chandler in August 2022. During this gap of it sitting in the inbox, there was another REQ-00185693 Urgent request to provide guidance for 6240M46 and 6240M49. Larry said that the REQ must have not been signed off and that he would like this REQ to still be approved. 

He also suggested that instead of 17-20SV-06 that we instead use 17-20SV-69 due to the inclusion of a Test Specification Sheet on pg 47 for 6240M4 that includes specs for sensitivity, TI tolerance, and what calibration sticker to put. This spec sheet is also useful because it is reference in Table 1 of the Procedure. METPRO lists 17-20SV-69 as one of the standards that can be used for 6240M4 along 17-20SV-06. 

Further research into the 6240M46 Spec sheet reveals that main difference between M4, M46, and M49 models is the length and type of cable. The specification for the accelerometer should not be affected by the cables. The spec sheet from Meggitt lists M83723/89Y for the connector type, SDB uses 2-pin cannon connector (F) 10-32 microdot as an older type of connection.

The standard 8B6 Lab Standard Accelerometer has a range of 10Hz to 10kHz, the uncertainty is dependent on the Report of Calibration. The latest number for uncertainty came from 2019 which has an average of 0.09% and there is another from 2014 which has 1.2 % as the average. Proper procedure is to go through Jessica who will direct you to James Wagner who will be able to provide the latest ROC.
 
Looking at the database, there was never a checklist that was created for this item. The format for this REQ uses a Test Specification Sheet.

A little information about TI. A piezoelectric accelerometer is used specifically for vibration testing. Sensitivity of an accelerometer defines at what rate the sensor converts mechanical energy into an electric signal. This defines the acceleration measurement range of the accelerometer. The unit of sensitivity is pC/g (picocoulombs per g) where g is the acceleration due to gravity.

POC: Brian Gibson, Gibson, Brian K Jr CIV USN FRCSW (USA) <brian.k.gibson34.civ@us.navy.mil>
TEInst:
Metrology Engineering at FRCSW has determined for TI model: STARA1210 [CAGE Code: 30260] Orion Star A121 Portable pH Meter should be user verified on a 12 month interval and is to be calibrated through a outside calibration lab.

Note 1: SDB does not currently have the capability to support this asset.

Note 2: COMSP will be submitted for the pH Meter. Until then, MATLAB will continue to do their calibration verification. Once COMSP is approved, MATLAB can calibrate the pH Meter.

Note 3: Current recommendation for outside calibration lab is Micro Quality Calibration Inc. which supports both pH meter and electrode.
TitleTicket: Orion Star A121 Portable pH Meter
WorkNotes:
The purpose of this REQ-00190143 it to provide User Cal verification for Materials Lab. They are looking to have us verify that there is no problems with their calibration and also get a User Cal sticker. The reasoning that they are sending this into SDB is because they have a new Quality Manager that is looking to get their TI’s calibrated and one of those instruments first get cal support is the Orion Star A121 pH Meter. The reasoning for a User Cal is that they use it once to twice a week, so they calibrate it monthly. There is verification or reasoning yet for why they use a monthly calibration. What they use to verify if they need to calibrate is when the pH buffer gives them a different reading, if that is the case they would recalibrate. 

STARA1210 or Orion Star A121 pH Meter will be used to measure the pH of the salt water in a Salt Water Fog Chamber for the purpose of R&D testing of metal. The pH range that is used to verify the salt water is 6 pH to 8 pH and that is referenced in their own suggested testing manuals and instructions. To calibrate the pH Meter for the specified pH range, two pH buffer solution one of pH 6 and another of pH 8 is used to help set up the pH meter. The reason that pH 6 and pH 8 is used is because they fall as very close to the range that the meter is measuring. If the buffer used in the measurement range is farther apart such as 4, 7 and 10 then that would lead to larger inaccuracy as stated by Brian. There is currently no plans to have a greater range for pH.

For actual steps of their current set up method, they go through the “calibration” process that is provided by Thermo Scientific. This procedure can be found in the folders. First step of the process is that the user would enter the calibration menu and then measure both the buffers that they are using. From the two points, the pH meter analyzes the pH, temperature, and mV to find a “slope.” The slope is measured in pH/mV, and the pH Meter displays the percentage of the measured value that falls within the theoretical value. If the percentage slope that is displayed is greater than 93% then it is passes the calibration step and is ready to accurately measure pH. They obtained the 93% requirement from a measurement tool provided from Thermo Scientific that recommends a 93% slope for a good measurement, this can be seen in the email and also the pH Theory from Thermo Scientific. 

To get a User Cal, there needs to be a transfer standard that is applicable to Orion Star A121. There will be a need to get the buffer solution verified and supported by NIST before submitting COMSP documents to get the standard buffer solution approved. There might be a problem in the future for calibration because the standard that is used is consumable. That means that if LabChem (producer of the solution) decides to not produce the solution any more there would be no possibility to calibrate. LabChem has also responded back with a Certificate of Analysis that says that the buffer solution is calibrated to NIST SRMs.

A User Cal procedure will also need to be written. The current plan is to implement the user cal provided by Thermo Scientific as a set up process for the TI Meter. For the actual procedures, the similar ICP procedures will be incorporated. The only issue is that these ICPs include testing other measurement points including temperature and millivolts. If that is the case, then they would not be able to perform calibration as Material Labs does not have the standards to calibrate it to that extent. If the ICP procedure is used, it will have to be modified to fit the needs of the STARA1210.

This REQ might represent a bit of a challenge due to the lack of recent ICP’s that have been created for pH meters. Similar ICP’s that have been written in the past include SC-42 and SC-44 that were last written in 1998. There is also no CPAR submissions that involve pH Testers. The pH buffer standards that were used in SC-42 and SC-44 are also listed as ancillary, so it might not be applicable. METPRO also has a similar model STARA3240N1 that was listed as User Cal. So there is there should be possibility to get User Cal since there were similar models used in the past and Materials Lab is not using to directly test warfighter components.

Another instrument that used to help measure is the measurement probe Orion 8107UWMMD ROSS Ultra pH/ATC Triode which has its own uncertainty and precision. This probe is able to measure temperature and mV. It must also be stored in special gel to keep the electrode inside from drying. To verify if the electrode is working, they use the same methodology as the TI where if the measurement readings of the buffer solutions are off, then they would go in figure out if there is a need to replace. The buffer solution also has a shelf life of around 1-2 years, so the solution is verified before use and bought again as necessary to verify.

Update 8/30
ICP SC-42 will be used since it allows guidance for any pH Meter that has a tolerance to better than 0.3%. To follow this procedure, will have to confirm with Brian Gibson if tolerance to can be increased to follow the ICP. Confirming with Mike, SDB is able to only support 392M digital thermometer.

For Voltage measurement, a substitute will have to made for Valhalla with a Fluke 5700 or equivalent. Since the electrode that is supplied with the TI is requires a solution to measure voltage, a BNC connector will have to be used with the BNC port of STARA1210 to connect it to the 5700. Will have to bring the pH meter from MATLAB over to SDB to confirm if they have a connector.

For temperature measurement, the ICP calls for a temperature chamber dry well. The previous ICP uses a ATC temperature probe to measure temperature. Today’s current technologies combines an electrode and temperature probe into a triode that measures pH, temperature, and voltage. For SDB to calibrate, they will have to use a liquid well to make measurements with included triode.

Request ICP correction to CPAR db# 16843 for p/n EK2000I Compact Balance.   ICP 17-20MM-08 for balances should be the cal procedure used instead of ICP 17-20MM-18 (using Class C weights) that is currently listed.

WorkNotes:
Background: Original CPAR entry dated back to 2008 where a checklist was submitted. In 2013 there was a need to update the CPAR entry to include a LCP-SDB-005-13. A request came back in 2015 for calibration saying that the LCP was incorrect as it damaged the standards and TI.

REI-CAL-15-0087: “Also refer to 15-SS-6512.
The true air speed indicator test set was being calibrated using LCP-SDB-005-13.  At step 4.1, the technician followed the step-by-step procedure outlined in the LCP before the transformer blew up and automatically shut down the calibrator.  The problem originated at the TI output at J1-B when power is applied at the output instead of the input. The voltage should've been applied across J1 pins A and F.  Based on passdown from calibration technicians, Code 600 Engineers tried to repair the unit and retest it only resulting in damages to other components. Based on the feedback from calibration managers and technicians, they have speculation that the engineers were modifying the circuit or trying to find a suitable replacement of obsolete components.     
METCAL ISEA was called upon for an urgent assist, but the TI was already broken. METCAL ISE rescinded LCP-SDB-005-13 because it was NOT technically sound and could cause potential harm to personnel or damage to equipment. Although the LCP was approved, the LCP was not properly verified/validated by our QA team.  The instruction directed the technician to apply a voltage using the calibrator 5700 at the output of a step-down transformer - this is not appropriate to apply power at an output. The power applied to the transformer can potentially blow up because it is not designed to handle the power draw.  

METCAL ISEA wrote up a draft LCP to correctly calibrate the AC voltmeter and the DC ammeter, however, it requires bench testing of the same model.  Since the item was rejected and being repaired, the REI was closed and the technician was recommended to resubmit another REI when a working unit is made available. “
EMAIL:
“
First, we need to set up the initial conditions and apply the stimulus at the appropriate pins. In the current LCP‐SDB‐005‐13 para 4.1, the 5700 calibrator is being set up to apply an AC Voltage at the output of TI, pins B and F. This setup is INCORRECT and can cause damage to the test instrument and the test equipment, but more importantly personnel getting hurt. Instead, the 5700 calibrator should apply the AC Voltage across pins A and F with S1 and S2 set to measure the AC Voltage. 

Also in LCP‐SDB‐005‐13 para 4.2, the switches (S1 and S2) needs to be configured correctly before the 5700 calibrator applies current via pins A and F.

Either way, bench testing using a modified LCP is required before officially releasing the LCP. At this time, the current LCP‐SDB‐005‐13 has been rescinded. At least, the checklist aligns with ICP 17‐20AQ‐147 and 17‐20SJ‐48 to calibrate the voltmeter, ammeter, and knots indicator.
“

Current status is to use a non-standard multimeter and measure the output voltage and current of the J1 connector. From there, if there is no output then a source will be applied at those connections. Caution should also be taken to make sure that IN/OUT Switch is at correct position. There will also be a need to verify that the pin connections are correct on the TI, for example if Pin A’s location is in the correct position from the LCP. An inspection will also be done to make sure that the TI’s electronic circuit has not been tampered with.

If TI is viable, then interim guidance will be given while LCP is written for long term support.
StatusTicket: Current LCP is not viable, no documentation supporting current calibration procedures. Currently researching past documents for evidence supporting LCP procedure and specifications/numbers that support TI requirements. Contact Rick, Terence, Baylon 4 info

ProbDesc: PLEASE PROVIDE PROCESS AND PROCEDURES TO LOCALLY PERFORM CALIBRATION/VERIFICATION ONLASER TRACKER MODEL LEICA, AT960-LR. ORIGINAL REQUEST WAS APPROVED UNDER BENEFICIALSUGGUSTION - #2000001. FRCSW HAS UPGRADED OUR LASER TRACKERS FROM THE LEICA AT901-B. THISPREVIOUS MODEL FRCSW PERFORMED A LOCAL CALIBRATION/VERIFICATION AT THE CALIBRATIONLAB USING ESTABLISHED PROCUDERES (17-20MD-234). PLEASE REACH OUT TO BEN BUTLER AND FRCSWREVERSE ENGINEERS (LANCE LEE, DAVID PRICE) FOR FURTHER QUESTIONS, COMMENTS, CONCERNSWITH THIS REQUEST. benjamin.butler37.civ@us.navy.mil lancelot.lee.civ@us.navy.milrichard.d.price81.civ@us.navy.mil
Resolution: Further research will be conducted in next REQ for this item to deterimine long term capability for calibraiton at SDB.
TEInst:
AT960-LR falls within the category of “Leica Laser Tracker” under the NAVAIR METCAL Authorized Service Provider List. AT960-LR is authorized for calibration under Hexagon, please send item to Hexagon for calibration.

Please send in another request for METCAL at FRCSW to do further investigation into capability of calibration at SDB and getting long term support.
WorkNotes:
Engineering Notes AT960-LR
Spoke with Lance from Reverse Engineering with regards to ticket. Technically the AT960-LR has the same uncertainty as AT901-B that is used in 17-20MD-234. There were two concerns that must be taken into account before allowing the use of 17-20MD-234 to be applied to the new laser tracker. The first concern is that the previous calibration guidance used a max range of 6.5 meters, the problem would be that Lance is trying to get it calibrated up to 60 meters. The TI tolerance of 54µm is dependent on the range that the item is measured from. The second concern is that the ICP set process specifically lists the At901. 

Another small concern is that the uncertainty of the Brunson 1.5LTE-1000MM is inconsistent across the year, so care must be taken when using the standard.
In terms of urgency, Lance has the option to continue calibrating with Hexagon, the seller of the laser tracker, for the next four years. So there is no urgency to calibrate it, but the option for him to calibrate comes in December.

It looks like Sean Murphy believes that we do not have the capabability to calibrate this item and that it would be a COMSP.

Fruther research into ASME B89.4.19 revealed that a minimum length of 2.3 meters is required for the length of the scale bar. The current standard is 1 meter. B89.4.19 also references a systems test and a range test. The systems test is what is currently in the ICP, but the range test is not included. The range test is used to compare the distance that is measured by the laser tracker with the reference bar length. NIST documentation on ASME B89.4.19 believes that the systems test (two face test) is significant enough for calibration. The NIST document does reference the need for a 2.3 meter length scale bar.

I think it would be possible to locally calibrate this so long as the scale bar has a length of at least 2.3 meters and a tolerance smaller than 13.5 µm. The specification of the Leica AT901-B matches AT960-LR. So if the ICP is considered still good, then AT960-LR could possibly be applied to it or substituted.

ProbDesc:
The Materials Engineering Lab requests authorization to implement limited internal, periodic calibration of the subject equipment. A common microstructural failure mechanism in high strength steels is hydrogen embrittlement. This mechanism is typically initiated when steel parts are electroplated and the plating parameters are not adequately controlled. The Mechanical Test group of the FRCSW Materials Engineering Lab tests for hydrogen embrittlement in electroplated components using three ATS 2330 Lever Arm units (see 2300_r2 Lever Arm Testers). The units apply load to a test specimen through a balanced beam with a 20:1 leverage ratio. Dead weight is stacked on a weight pan suspended from the long arm of the lever and a fixed specimen is attached to the short arm. Accuracy of load transfer is a function of unit geometry, primarily the precise distances between the fulcrum and load axes at each end of the lever. Unit operation is described in draft SOP MT-035-21_Final. The Lever Arm units are large and heavy, and cannot easily be moved. Movement can also affect geometry and impact calibration. Calibration of the units is best accomplished on-site. Unit calibration can be simply accomplished by comparison of applied load (dead weight plates) with readout from a Secondary (force) Standard. Because of the simplicity of load application, unit calibration can be accomplished by comparison of applied load (dead weight plates) with readout from a Secondary (force) Standard installed in place of a test specimen. User calibration is viable as long as: 1) The Secondary Standard is periodically compared with a Primary Standard; 2) A comprehensive calibration process is applied; and 3) Individuals performing calibration have a thorough understanding the mechanics of load application, including direction, rate, motive force, force transmission, and force multiplication, for the testing system. In preparation for internal calibration, the Materials Engineering Lab, Code 494, has: 1) Developed an internal calibration protocol for the calibration of the ATS 2330 Lever Arm units; 2) Integrated the protocol in the Laboratories Quality Program; 3) Acquired a load cell (Interface Model 1220AF-25K-B ); 4) Submitted the Standard to MetCal for periodic calibration per NAVAIR 17-20MF-08 (Current calibration record is attached).

WorkNotes:
Toshio confirmed that they would need to full range for the customer. To allow for this full range, ICP 17-20MM-18 would need to be used instead to allow the full range of 150 kg or 331 lb.

After discussing with Toshio, they are able to use the other standards that are called out in the ICP. 

Special calibration label will need to be affixed to the TI because the scale is not able to accomadate the shift test that is called out in 4.1.7 in the ICP. There shouldn't be able any problem with this since 4.1.5 calls out to use a special cal if the standards do not fit the shift test. Confirmation of this can be seen in the email in the folder where Toshio confirmed that the 50lb weight standards are 14cmx20cm. This takes up more than a quarter of the space on the Digital Platform Scale, the platform scale is around 26cmx26cm.

17-20MM -18 will be used instead of MM-08 because it is able to fit the full range of the ICP. MM- 18 was originally not considered (as seen in the REQ problem statement) because Generic Calibration Guidance was not applicable to this. GCG allows for tolerances greater than 1%, but CS100 is 0.3%. Upon closer inspection, GCG can not be applied but the ICP itself can because there are items with similar tolerances that are called out in the Appendix.

AKI and AKF also confirmed with the customer that they would be using this for general purpose and would not be used for specific aircraft.

12 month interval will be used in accordance with GCG (not using GCG though). MUA does allow for a 24 month interval.

Another possible concern with regards to MUA is that the tolerance used 0.03% is separate from the resolution. If resolution is accounted for also, the accuracy would be too tight for the resolution and would cause the MUA to not ouput. So for the purpose of the MUA, it will be assumed that the accuracy already includes the resolution in the uncertainty budget. There is not enough documentation from the supplier to confirm if that accuracy has resolution already built into it or not.

ProbDesc: The Metrology Requirements List, NAVAIR 17-35MTL-1 (METPRO/MTRL), lists the L. S. Starrett Co. (57163) model 128, Inside Micrometer procedures as 17-20MD-09, 17-51MD-009, and 17-20MD-11, to calibrate the 2 inch vernier, least gradient 0.001 inch, head micrometer and the a Dial Indicator, range 0.1000 inch with a least gradient 0.0005 inch, however the procedure does not work for calibrating Combination Head Master or the Setting Master, inside dimension 9.999x inch ±0.0002 inch. The Combination head uses the dial indicator as pressure instrument to make sure that each measurement is at the same pressure to increase accuracy. The Setting master is use to set the Combination head to an exact value before testing. These two pieces are the 128. The 128AZ which is the rest of the set is a normal inside micrometer and could be calibrated using 17-xxMD-09 if not for the fact that it is part of a set with the 128 Combination Head. Each rod should be set to a correct length with the combination head after setting the combination head with the setting master. Only then should you use the micrometer head from the 128AZ and adjust it to match the adjusted rods. In addition, the 17-xxMD-09s do not cover a 2 inch Vernier. We will need a procedure that address that there are two sets that must be calibrated together, how to calibrate the setting master, how to set the combination head with a 2 inch Vernier, then calibrate it (most likely using pieces from the 128AZ), and then the calibration of the 128AZ. We will need to figure out what tolerances to calibrate it to and what test equipment to use. The L. S. Starrett Co. (57163) website, https://www.starrett.com, lists the model 128 as an inch-reading Combination Head with Setting Master Combination Head with Setting Master. The inch-reading Combination Head with Setting Master Combination Head is a 2 inch vernier, least gradient 0.001 inch, head micrometer attached to a frame holding a Dial Indicator, range 0.1000 inch with a least gradient 0.0005 inch, see attached picture. The Setting Master is the Combination Head Master, inside dimension 9.999x inch ±0.0002 inch.
Resolution: Interim guidance. Will follow up with LCP draft development.

Simply purchasing a new scale bar would not be enough as a new procedure would have to be made for the calibration of that scale bar and it would also have to get approval for use. After talking with Brunson instruments (manufacturer of the scale bar), they stated that this scale bar methodology does not replace an OEM's level of calibration and that their scale bars are used simply for a quick piece of mind check after delivery. We also do not have the currently have the lab environment to test the laser tracker's max distance of 70-80 meters which might be affected by vibration, temperature, and outside factors in the field.
WorkNotes:
Currently stuck between following COMSP route or to go with giving support. There are other labs that are following COMSP route for this item as seen in MEASURE. This would be the easy route and allow this REQ to close. The reason that we want to do long term support is that CH-53 IMP Production Manager Benjamin Butler states that the current COMSP Procedure is costly and they have to drive up to Los Angeles to drop off the item and pick it up for calibration. Doing an in house procedure would save around $90,000 dollars a year in calibration costs.

A bit of background into how the calibration of a laser tracker works. There is a laser beam that is outputted from the laser tracker that hit an object an returns back to the tracker, from there the tracker is able to determine the length of the object. For the current calibration method as stated in 17-20MD-234, a scale bar with spherical balls on both ends are used as reference length for the laser tracker.

The only obstacle to developing a procedure is that there is not enough technical knowledge to justify the current standard that SDB has which is a 1 meter scale bar. NIST and ASME documents state at least a 2.3 meter length scale bar to be used, but our lab only has a 1m scale bar. There is also a small concern with measurement distance of the laser tracker. Previous laser tracker had a measurement distance of 6 meters from the bar, but the trackers range is higher than that at 80 meters. The CRA for AT901 did not state where they got that specific range and ASME justification for the length of the bar.

Current conclusion from the investigation leads me to believe that COMSP route will have to continue to be implemented due to lack of technical justification for procedures called out in CRA for 17-20MD-234 that would have been utilized for this REQ. Possible solutions that could change this would be if in the future, our team was able to get a hold of the Hexagon (Leica)'s internal calibration procedure or if there is a possible laser tracker SME that could justify the steps for laser trackers.

In document "Fr M. Lee to ET, Hexagon 12 recommendation" of 21B0641 Equipment Jacket, there is a reference to a calibration lab that received Hexagon's calibration procedures during an audit for their COMSP approval. If we were able to access this procedure, then this might allow the Navy to internally calibrate Laser Trackers in the future.

Current challenge with AMAD Calibraiton is that calibration of the torque cell poses safety risks for the operator. Past AMAD tests stands relied on a hydraulic jack to increase apply different amounts of force against the torque cell. That hydraulic jack is not longer operable as the legs are curved, no longer sit flush with the bottom of the floor.

Current needs of the calibration stand is to have a device that varies height of the torque cell. Current space of the bottom of the test stand is small around 8"x8". The amount of torque that would be applied is around 1800in-lb. IF the the torque arm is around 40 in long then by calculation of Torque = Force x Length, then 40lbf.

Solutions that were used to counteract this obstacle was to find varying metal plates and twobyfours of various thicknesses that would allow this heigh adjustments. Safetly concern is that it is very cumbersome to enter the test stand and place these plates. Stacking plates is also unstable as a large amount of force is need to apply against the torque cell. 

There are various solutions to this. One idea would be drill holes into the concrete attach an adjustable rod to the base of the test stand. There are also ideas to 3D print a scissor lift out of plastic. The only concerns is that an 3D printed part would not be tall and strong enough to withstand the torque applied. Another concern is that there is not funding in place to create a fixture to fix this problem.

ProbDesc: NOTE: THICKNESS VERIFICATION OF RADAR ABSORBABLE MATERIALS (RAM) IS CRITICAL TO COMPONENT AND AIRCRAFT PAINT SHOP PRODUCTION PROCESSES. RESTORATION OF RAM ON DAMAGED INLET DUCT WILL REACH A WORK STOP IF EQUIPMENT CAPABILITY IS NOT STOOD UP BY RDD. The PosiTector 6000 FNS3, is a digital thickness gauge that uses eddy current and magnetic induction to measure PR-2460, an elastomeric material with ferrous particles, whose material composition and properties are proprietary and classified by Boeing. The PosiTector has been proven to work on PR-2460 and NOT on PR-2414. The FNS3 advanced model, can be programmed to via a Non NMCI computer and a polynomial function. The PosiTector with FNS3 probe has been procured by Materials Engineering Department and requires induction into the FRCSW Calibration Program. Calibration Lab does not have calibration instructions specific to the programmable PosiTector 6000 intended for PR-2460 ONLY. More information on the equipment is provided below: This equipment is used to measure the dry film thickness of the RAM coating (PR-2460). Measuring the thickness of the material is a critical step in the production process since the thickness is used as an evaluation for rework to obtain the coating thickness tolerances established for the specified nominal thickness. The PosiTector has been used for samples of PR-2460 that range between 18 - 45 mils in dry film thickness. The equipment we want to calibrate has instructions from DeFelsko on how to input the curve. I created one locally and Jacksonville NAS has sent me a copy of their curves, both of which worked to create the polynomial necessary to measure the thickness accurately.
TEInst: incorrect routing, return to sender.

The uncertainty for this weight could probably be tightened in the future to get a loose uncertainty requirement for the torque arm.

TEInst:
Metrology Engineering at FRCSW authorizes SDB to calibrate TI A-LE-X-1-1-0-0-1-1-0-1-0-2-0-0-0-C (CAGE code: 8F723) LE REFRIGERANT MONITOR with the following guidance:
Procedure: 17-20SY-43

Range: 0 to 1000 ppm
Tolerance: ±250ppm
Interval: 9 months
Checklist: see ICP 17-20SY-43 for LE Refrigerant 10196612 checklist

Note: Ensure that certified gas standards Matheson Tri-Gas GMT2700731TD, GMT2700732TD, and GMT2700733TD are acquired before next cal cycle to ensure long term support for this item.
WorkNotes:
Model: A-LE-X-1-1-0-0-1-1-0-1-0-2-0-0-0-C
ALEX1100110102000C
CAGE: 8F723
CPAR DB#20745

9 Month interval came from METRL for ALEX1100110102000C and 10196612

Table 1 requirement of 250PPM mostly likely came from the original ICPs for Freon Indicators 3290 and 3890 which lists that tolerance and was created in 1986.

Concerns with Table 1 tolerance of 20SY-43 being ±250PPM versus 17-50MX-071 with tolerances between ±10PPM to ±81PPM. After further research there is a concern with how a gap there is in tolerance between the two different procedures. MUA was used to calculate the combined tolerances of 20SY-43 standards. In the future, Matheson Tri-Gas Standards should be acquired to meet latest industry standards. 20SY-43 does not meet the requirements of manufacturer's specifications. It might be difficult to get this long term supported since there might be engineering concerns with the discrepencies in tolerance between manufacturer specs and the old ICP. The old ICP also lacks a test point below 100 ppm which has a tighter tolerance than 100-1000ppm range. New ICP accounts for this lack of test point. Old ICP is also incorrect in that the range of the item should start at 20 ppm and not 0ppm.

Another important information in terms of nomenclature is that Refrigerant Monitor 10196612 (called out in 17-20SY-43) is the same item as ALEX1100110102000C. The only difference is that 10196612 is the NAVSEA equivalent of our NAVAIR item.

This is a one time authorization. 

Visiting SDB, it was found that the only gas standard that was acquired was GMT2700731TD which only covered the 100ppm range of the item. Other two gas standards were missing and never arrived. Another missing ancillary item is Mine Safety 467896 Flow controller, this should not be a concern though as SDB has equivalent flowmeters to use.

History Investigation - Table 1 of 17-20SY-43 requirement of 250PPM most likely came from the original ICPs for Freon Indicators 3290 and 3890 which use and was created in 1986.

Recommend to use old method until new gas standards come in before next cal cycle.

ProbDesc: The Dial Caliper Gage 209-351 cage code S3257 and other associated model numbers are not in METPRO, but there is a procedure available. Procedure 17-20MD-80 is for External and internal diameter Dial Calipers.  I also request to work on the current one using the manufactures specs (Range: 0.20 to 0.60, Tolerance: +/- 0.0008 IN. Resolution: 0.0002 IN.) and 17-20MD-80
TEInst:
Metrology Engineering at FRCSW authorizes SDB to calibrate TI 209-351 (CAGE code: J4271) INTERNAL DIAL CALIPER GAGE with the following guidance:

Procedure: 17-20MD-80

Range: 0.20 to 0.60 in.

Tolerance: ±0.0008 in.

Resolution: 0.0002 in.

Interval: 24 months

Checklist: TEI-00241587-17-20MD-80_Checklist

Bench Test is required. Blank BT form is attached and will need to be filled out and signed by calibrator as part of CPAR Package requirement
WorkNotes:
This is a new item that is looking to get calibrated. CPAR Submission will be needed as this is an R coded asset.

A visual inspection of the TI picture leads to the conclusion that TI is an internal dial caliper. This means that is used to measure the internal diameters of objects such as inner pipe diameter or inner diameter of conclave object. This distinction is necessary as internal caliper steps are different than external caliper steps in the reference NAVAIR ICP 17-20MD-80.

UUT Tolerance of ±0.0008 in was derived from specification from 209-351 Dial Caliper manufacturer's specification sheet. There is also a graduation of 0.0002 that will be used as the resolution of the TI. 

TDME uncertainties was taken from Table 1 of 17-20MD-185 Gage Blocks for Grade 2 with NIST's "The Gage Block Handbook" used as a fact check. Starrett SS88A1X gage blocks are calibrated to Grade 2 Tolerances as seen their respective METRL entries. All gage blocks that will be used for this calibration are under 1 inch in length. As seen in section 2.2.3 under NIST's Gage block handbook, the lower tolerance will be 2µin and upper tolerance will be 4µin. All measurement points can be done with 2 gage blocks taken from SS88A1X. Two gage block jaws will also be used for the outside external measurement. In total there would be 4 gage blocks under 1 inch length that are Grade 2 tolerance. Gage blocks available for use can be found in the SS88A1X METRL specification page. Root sum square (RSS) will be done for four gage blocks incorporating Grade Tolerance to account for errors when wringing gage blocks. This RSS calculation (seen in the bottom right of this MUA) yields a low tolerance value of 2.828427 µin and a upper tolerance of 5.656854 µin

TDME resolution was taken from manufacture specification sheet which state a graduation of 0.0002in. This will be applied as the TI's resolution. 

Measurement points were taken based on 17-20MD-80 which suggests a minimum of 8 points throughout the major graduations. From the picture of the TI, the major graduations happen at increments of 0.04 in.

Interval of 24 months will be used as is based on similar dial caliper in METRL under same Mitutoyo Cage code S3257 under model 209-552 and falls under the same 209 series. 

In terms of policy, it can be argued that Generic Calibration Guidance 17-35MTL-1 using ICP 17-20MD- 07 can be applied to this TI considering it falls under the range and tolerance. From a user and cal technician standpoint, 20MD-07 is not specific and is more catered towards large length calipers. 20MD-07 does not have specific directions like MD-80 for small measurement items that measure micro inches. There is not significant differences between the two procedures, 20MD-80 is favorable since it provides a clearer steps of these type of inside dial caliper gages.

Checklist will not be provided as ICP provides sample checklist and instructions for technicians to choose test points that they find most easiest to work with.

ProbDesc:
Request calibration guidance for the Humidity/Temperature probe.

ICP 17-20MH-33
EngNotes: Currently working on proofreading CPAR before submission.
TEInst:
Metrology Engineering at FRCSW authorizes SDB to calibrate TI PCMini52-S+4+H+X (CAGE code: 0CYH4) HUMIDITY AND TEMPERATURE MINI PROBE with the following guidance:

Procedure: 17-20MH- 33
Range: 0 to 100%RH
Tolerance: ±2.4%RH
Interval: 12 months
Checklist: TEI-00241630-17-20MH-33_Checklist.pdf

Note 1: Apply Special Calibration sticker for ±2.4%RH and for no temperature calibration. 
Note 2: Suggest placing probe vertical for possible better humidity readings. 
Note 3: Please send back completed Meter Card and Bench Test checklist for CPAR Submission.
Note 4: Ensure power supply is supplying between 6-35Vdc.
WorkNotes:
Humidity probe is part of the 7532001 Bauer Motor Driven Fan Test Stand. Only humidity will be measured as test stand does not require temperature, this requirement is also listed on the probe itself. 

Current challenges posed by the probe is that is is currently reading around below 4-8%RH the expected humidity tolerance of ±2%RH. Special cal will have to be done and loosened to ±2.4%RH to CATII requirements from Bauer's test stand manual. ±2%Rh would be ideal as that is Rotronic's specifications for the tolerance. Routes have been explored to manually change the resistance value on the probe so that it reads a linearized 5V/%RH instead of the current 4.8V/%RH. Software challenges prevented this adjustement to be made. Emails with Bauer and Rotronics at suggestions for suggestions on calibration improvements did not yield an fruitful insights. Manufacturer suggestions were to send it to the OEM manufacturer for 

Full range of 0 to 100%RH will be used as that gives a higher tolerance when doing the calculations for the voltage conversion of voltage to humidity on the DMM during calibration. It could be argued that 10-90%RH is the true tolerance, but that will be not be used as that gives a inaccurate conversion ratio when applying the voltage to humidity conversion equation in 17-20MH-33.

Power supply does not affect the voltage readings from the humidity probe. So long as the humidity probe is being supplied with between 6Vdc to 35Vdc, then that should be enough to power the probe.

Interval of 12 months came from like models in CPAR such as GXL and F2CW420 which also Rotronic models. This interval is also favored since the test stand that this supports is also on a 12 month cycle.

WorkNotes:
The Taylor Inst. 21001 THERMOMETER (p.o. Taylor Inst. 21009 PRECISION THERMOMETER) that the customer is requesting to substitute has a tolerance of ±0.1 °C according to its calibrating ICP (both 17-20ST-253 and 17-20ST-195) and a prescribed "minimum use" range of 19 to 21 °C from the SS88A1X/SS8A1X calibrating ICP (17-20MD-185/17-51MD-185).

"Note: … if the temperature at the comparator has increased by 0.1 °C or more, it may be advisable to step away from the operation until the effect of body heat has dissipated."

ProbDesc:
AKF do not have a traceable 20A measurement method due to NPSL limitations.
ICP 17-20AQ-538 requires having current shunt with calibrated current shunt value (up to 20Amps), but NPSL provided report (ROC) cannot support them at 20Amps as limited (ROC is supporting up to 18Amps).
Requesting to use 18Amps value instead of 20 Amps as used as accept 18 Amps deviation value of ROC provided. Please refer to TEI-00086697.
TEInst:
Metrology Engineering at FRCSW will return this REQ for the following reason(s):

1)  Recommend sending Y5020 Current Shunt back for calibration to NPSL. NPSL has recently acquired a new 8100 Clarke Hess Transconductance Amplifier that would allow calibration up to 20A. Guidance can not be given for use at 20A using Report of Calibration tolerance at 18A due to linearity relationship between voltage and current. The tolerance might differ significantly at 20A if not calibrated.
WorkNotes:
AKI/AKF is looking to confirm if they are able to calibrate their 5220A Transconductance Amplifier with the Y5020A Current Shunt which seems to have a limited range of 18A dc instead of the expected 20A dc. This limited range of 18 A dc has supposedly been the case for more than 10 years at NPSL due to the limited range of the old standard Fluke 5220A Transconductance Amplifier of 20A dc. To calibrate Y5020 you would need to supply more than 20A dc due to some of the current being lost.

For long term plan, NPSL has recently acquired a new 8100 Clarke Hess Amplifier that allows calibration up to 100A dc which would more than cover the 20A dc full range of Y5020. It also seems that this capability recently came into place and there was an oversight with updating the range of Y5020 form 18A to 20A dc.

For the short term guidance, it was confirmed through NPSL and NIST that there is not a significant difference in the resistance values at 18A dc and 20A dc for Y5020 Current Shunt.

Hopefully there will not be a need to have to escalate this. If ticket comes back and there is no updated RoC, recomend to submit and ISEA ticket to get Y5020 full calibrated to 20A dc.
StatusTicket: Currently conducting engineering investigation on when the Y5020 is not calibrated to full range of 20 amp at NPSL. Depending on whether this is a temporary or permanent change at NPSL, the guidance will be different.

ProbDesc:
