CPAR DB NO. 17917
TEInst:
This REQ is to provide clarification of the guidance provided in CPAR DB# 17917. 

Manufacturer specifications for Model: 7259B-25 (cage: 95411) accelerometer are as follows:
Nominal Sensitivity:  25.0 mV/g ±10%
Frequency Response: ± 1dB of measured sensitivity @ 100Hz
Amplitude Linearity: ±1%
Bias Voltage: 10 V dc ±1.5 V dc

The CPAR form in the attached CPAR database entry suggests the following:
Nominal Calibration Sensitivity: 25.0mV/g, ± 10% of the nominal sensitivity
Frequency Response: ± 5% of the measured sensitivity at 100 Hz
Amplitude Linearity: ± 1% deviation between the measured values at the low and high amplitude
Bias Voltage: 10 V dc ± 1.5 V dc

The CPAR suggested tolerance was not accepted, the final acceptance of tolerances in CPAR DB# 17917 are as follows:
Nominal Calibration Sensitivity: 25.0mV/g, ± 10% of the nominal sensitivity
Frequency Response: ± 10% of the measured sensitivity at 100 Hz
Amplitude Linearity: ± 1% deviation between the measured values at the low and high amplitude
Bias Voltage: 10 V dc ± 1.5 V dc

Though the CPAR guidance does not match exactly with the manufacturer’s specification, it is an assumed approximation of ±1 dB of measured sensitivity. 

The following equation is used to calculate ±1 dB:
=20*LOG(measured/nominal)
±1 dB for 25.0 mV/g equates to the following tolerances:
Frequency Response: +12.2%, -10.9%

If any of the test instrument fall outside of the ±10% measured sensitivity proposed in the CPAR guidance, submit another REQ to have the CPAR guidance superseded.

TEInst:
After investigation in the method in which Model: 72-6345-1 (CAGE: 07239) High Resistance Decade Box (Serial: 76990) is used in ICP 17-20AR-143 to calibrate Model: 1864-9700 (Serial Numbers: G3-19150814 and G3-20220857), Metrology Engineering at FRCSW has determined the Test Instruments do not need to be recalled.

17-20AR-143 ICP Table following step 4.3.2 uses the following calculation:

R𝑦=R1+R3+((R𝑠+R1 ) x R3)/R2
Where:
R1 and R3 are the 100 MΩ Decade Resistors
R2 is the 250KΩ Decade Resistor
Rs is an internal resistor in series with the Test Instrument circuit
and
Ry is the nominal 1TΩ resistance being verified (to ±7% TΩ)

The out of tolerance condition equates to 690 KΩ or 0.69% error contribution
This causes little to no impact on the Calculated TUR or PFA which is well below 2% (0.90%).

TEInst:
Metrology Engineering at FRCSW has determined that the OOT condition of TMDE model: HQS2X1 (CAGE Code: 28066, S/N: HQS-61700) Pressure Sensor Module has significantly impacted the quality of prior calibrations. The following test instruments must be recalled for calibration:

103601 (CAGE Code: 14487, S/N: MYM4031) Liquid Nitrogen Storage Tank
WorkNotes:
The UUT model 103601 (CAGE: 14487) Liquid Nitrogen Storage Tank was calibrated by TMDE model HQS2X1 (CAGE: 28066) Pressure Sensor Module which was found to be OOT. An MUA is performed to evaluate whether the OOT TMDE has a significant impact on the calibration of the UUT IAW NA 17-20MP-115.

The "OOT MUA" is based off of on "Original MUA" performed by Mr. Bradley Patyk on 03/26/2025 for the model 103600 (CAGE: 14487) Liquid Oxygen Tank in regards to ISEA ticket 26-00146. The model 103601 tank uses the same procedure and standards as the model 103600 tank.

Note that in the original MUA, a UUT tolerance of ±0.75% fs (fs = 47.5 inH2O) is used which does not agree with the tolerances stated in NA 17-20MP-115. 
Mr. Patyk specifies in his notes that the 0.75% fs tolerance is the correct tolerance based on his assesment of the UUT. However, the OOT MUA will use the tolerances as stated in the ICP to ensure that results are relevant to the procedure as it is written.

The nominal TMDE tolerance is ±0.07 inH2O, (converted from ±0.0051 inHg) k = 2. The OOT data, included on the last sheet of this document, shows that when the TMDE was calibrated, the "least OOT" test point had a difference between nominal and measured values of 1.34 inH2O. To capture the effect of the OOT TMDE in this MUA, the TMDE tolerance is therefore set to ±1.34 inH2O, k = 2. It is noted that using the "least OOT" test point error and using a k = 2 distribution both serve to underestimate the uncertainty caused by the OOT TMDE. 

Despite this, the result of the adjusted TMDE error is a severely low TUR and exceeded PFA/PFR limits for all test points. Therefore it is recommended that the UUT be recalled for calibration.

ProbDesc: Reference Attenuator, MN: 11708A, SN: 06782, assigned to SDB as a standard, found to be OOT IAW NA17-51GA-049, at one test point (OOT value attached). Please review traceability report to determine if any of the 22 remaining calibrations performed during the in-use time contain evidence of impact to quality or safety ERAR 2430456 has been closed and this REQ has been referenced.
TEInst:
Metrology Engineering at FRCSW has determined that the OOT finding for M/N: 11708A Reference Attenuator, SN: 06782 contains no evidence of impact to quality or safety.

The 22 TIs presented on the reverse traceability report are all power sensors (M/N: 8481D or 8484A) that utilized the
11708A Reference Attenuator in ICP 17-20GD-35MB for the "Reference Cal" preliminary step in conjunction with the TI's power meter (E4418B).

This Reference Cal has no effect on any of the calibration measurements for the TI: Connector Dimension, VSWR, Calibration Factor, Linearity.

The Calibration Factor test uses a different reference output which is set using the 1807A RF Power Standard, 1805B RF Control Unit, E8257DN01 Signal Generator, and 44-30 Fixed Coax Attenuator (with RoC). Power factors are calculated relative to the reference output set by these standards.

Linearity is measured by setting a reference output using the 5700ANV3SERIESII Calibrator and measuring the change in power level relative to the set reference output.

The only instance in which the OOT 11708A would make an impact is if the preliminary reference calibration was performed and utilized to make direct measurements, which is not the case for any of the 22 TIs.

In conclusion, it has been determined that no recall is necessary with respect to the OOT finding for M/N: 11708A Reference Attenuator, SN: 06782.
WorkNotes: The OOT standard was only used for the calibration of 8481D and 8484A power sensors using 17-20GD-35MB. The Reference Attenuator in question was only utilized in prelimary operations and had no effect on the calibration measurements of the TIs.
StatusTicket: Investigation performed to determine that no recall is necessary for the OOT standard.

WorkNotes:
Each instrument calibrated by the OOT 3689A that has an operational range inclusive of the OOT points indicated on ERAR 2630210 is given a single row in the MUA Document sheet to evaluate the effect that the OOT points has on that instrument's PFA. The result of the analysis (Recall/No Recall) is indicated in the first column of the sheet under "Section".

For each instrument, the worst-case OOT test point is used. 

TMDE
King Nutronics 3689A Precision Pressure Standard
Range:			N/A
Adjusted Unc.:		±|Actual Nom−1st Measurement|
Resolution:		Not included in unc. budget
Source:			ERAR 2630210
Confidence:		Normal, k=2
NCE Status:		N/A
ICP Use Code:	N/A

The adjusted TMDE uncertainty is assumed to be ±|Actual Nom−1st Measurement| as written on the ERAR.

The error limit distribution for the adjusted TMDE uncertainty is assumed to be rectangular. This is chosen because there is no available data to determine the behavior of the damaged TMDE (the METER card indicates that this unit was leaking air).

The adjusted TMDE uncertainty is assumed to be the dominant uncetainty contributor; all other sources of uncertainty (e.g., resolution, pressure head, etc.) are ignored for the purposes of this analysis. 

It was noted on the OOT METER card that the 3689A was leaking/damaged. Because the effect of this leak on measurements is likely not linear or exponential with respect to time, it would be improper to rely on the "reverse traceability date" estimation tool to determine dates before which the 3689A was in-tolerance. Therefore, all instruments found to have unacceptable PFA due to worsened 3689A performance are recalled.

ProbDesc: Torque Driver, Model: BFH040SAEV22, Cage: 09MR0 (MAKITA USA INC), with Set Point 40 lb.in, Tolerance: ±10% iv, is listed in METRL (04/01/2026) for using ICP 17-51MU-088 (1 NOV 2013). The procedure mandates the use of high-precision (±0.5%) calibration standards (Cell #2 and Cell #3 of TSDTFC2060EX001) to calibrate a low-precision (±10%) Unit Under Test (UUT) with TAR=20. The Makita Torque Driver is an industrial power-tool that operates at high speed (~400 RPM) and utilizes a mechanical clutch that creates a significant shock/impact load upon reaching its preset torque. While calibration standard is high-precision (±0.5%) and sensitive transducers designed for controlled, static load conditions. Using a highly sensitive laboratory instrument to calibrate a high-impact industrial power-tool is technically unsound. It creates an unacceptably high probability of transducer overload and catastrophic failure. This technical mismatch creates a high risk of damage to expensive standards due to the Test Instrument's high-speed, high-impact operation. Such damage would result in a complete workflow stoppage, halting all associated maintenance and production activities (the attached file “Technical Memorandum Issue 17-51MU-088” will support more detail explanation). Request to recommend two solutions to compromise this issue: • Temporary Short-Term Solution: We propose adjusting the local practice to utilize Cell #3 only for all Makita calibration steps. This meets all accuracy requirements while providing superior protection for the system's most sensitive components. • Long-Term Sustainable Solution (Decoupling): We recommend evaluating a standalone, ruggedized Torque Tester specifically for dynamic power tools. This "Decoupling" approach will permanently safeguard our high-end AKO standards and ensure 100% workflow availability for precision metrology. x
TEInst:
Metrology Engineering at FRCSW will return this REQ for the following reason(s):

He says that TI  BFH040SAEV22 Torque Driver is too rough to calibrated on Cell #2. There is currently no workload of BFH040SAEV22 to test or give short term guidance to. Ticket looks to be asking for long term support.

ProbDesc: HIGH COMPLIANCE MULTI-PRODUCT CALIBRATOR, MN: 5080AAN, SN: 4155810, assigned to SDB as a standard, found to be OOT IAW 17-20AX-1095MB, at 3 test points (OOT values attached). Please review traceability report to determine if the 376 True RMS Clamp Meter calibration performed during the in-use time contain evidence of impact to quality or safety. ERAR 2430295 has been closed and this REQ has been referenced.
TEInst:
Metrology Engineering at FRCSW has determined that the Out of Tolerance (OOT) finding for M/N: 5080AAN High Compliance Multi-Product Calibrator, S/N: 4155810, contains no evidence of impact to quality or safety.
The OOT finding was found using ICP 17-20AX-1095MB, during step 4.10.14, 4.10.24, and 4.10.26. These test points are for AC Current measurements at 60Hz, 300Hz, and 61Hz with errors of 0.26845%, -0.8986 mA, and -0.9279 mA respectively.
After reviewing the traceability report provided, the only TI calibration in need of analysis was for M/N: 376 True RMS Clamp Meter, S/N: 23630431. The TI was calibrated with ICP 17-20AQ-32. The 5080AAN is listed as item 2.1, 2.2, 2.3 and 2.4 of the ICP. The only section that would be potentially impacted by the OOT standard is section 4.3 Alternating Current Test. The only two test points that fall closest to the range of the OOT involves the standard output of 0.5 A at 60 Hz with a tolerance of ± 20 mA and 0.5 A at 400 Hz with a tolerance of ± 40 mA.
After performing a Measurement Uncertainty Analysis (MUA) of the worst case between the test points with the inclusion of the error from the OOT, the Probability for False Acceptance (PFA) was calculated to be 1.07% and Probability for False Rejection (PFR) was calculated to be 1.30%. The calculated values for PFA and PFR suggest that there is minimal impact on the calibration of the TI.
In conclusion, it has been determined that no recall is necessary with respect to the OOT finding for M/N: 5080AAN High Compliance Multi-Product Calibrator, S/N: 4155810.

ProbDesc: The procedure of 17-20MU-56 (01 MAY 2025) focuses on the calibration for the LEF Torque Calibration Kit (HR Textron P/N 84001060, 84001060-001, and 84001060-002, cage: 81873) with range 0-1,000 lbf.in, tolerance ±5 lbf.in (±0.5 % of Full Scale). From the perspective of metrology standards and physical principles, the procedure describes the dead-weight method to calibrate the LEF Torque Calibration Kit using the standard torque (TSD125H is the Substitute Standard of CTS2000P) and weights (D77). A comprehensive metrological review of the NAVAIR 17-20MU-56 procedure reveals critical technical omissions as follows: 1/ The procedure does not explicitly account for the effect of Earth's local gravitational acceleration (9.7951985 m/s2). This causes a permanent fixed deviation of -0.117%, which impact at 1,000 lb.in, the generated torque is 998.83 lb.in, resulting in a fixed negative bias of -1.13 lb.in. 2/ The procedure does not explicitly account for the effect of the calibrated length of the Lever Arm TSD125H, which recently is 10.014 in of side A and 10.020 in of side B. ProbDesc: According to NIST SP 811, (Torque and Work/Energy are distinct quantities) the unit of Torque represents as lb.in or lbf.in, and under the training document NAVAIR 17-35QAL-2, the unit of Torque also represents as lb.in (Chapter 8, item 8-2, page 367). But ICP 17-20MU-97 uses the unit as in-lb which is the unit of Work/Energy, to describe the Torque unit. By using in-lb, the ICP is using incorrect terminology according to formal USCS standards. Request to permit using lbf.in or lb.in as the Torque unit in the “Certificate of Calibration” for Torquemeter.
EngNotes: REQ must be handled through ISEA. Asking for ICP change.
TEInst:
Metrology Engineering at FRCSW has returned this REQ for the following reason(s):

1)  Requests to make changes to ICP cannot be done through REQ/TEI. Please submit a ticket to ISEA for resolution.

Note 1: Origin of Unit Discrepancies
The discrepancy in units most likely stems from the OEM (Original Equipment Manufacturer) specifications and historical Navy SOPs, which historically and currently use 'in-lb' and 'lb-in' interchangeably.

Note 2: Guidance on Short Substitution and Compliance
For short substitutions, it is strongly advised to maintain consistency with the units specified in the ICP (in-lb). Although the technical distinction between the two units is negligible, strict adherence to the documented procedure or Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is necessary to ensure audit compliance and maintain quality assurance standards. Consequently, the SDB Certificate of Calibration should reflect the specific units dictated by the ICP.
WorkNotes:
Asking to substitute nomenclature of in-lb for lb-in in the Certificate for Calibration for torque meter. Not done through us, would have to be CPR to have units of measurement changed in ICP 17-20MU-97. I don't see a problem as there is documentation to support this claim. This would not a immediate technical issue, but more of a preference in nomenclature. There is also support since in-lb doesn't necesarily support 17-35TR-50.

Personally, I think this would be a wasted effort to change all torque ICPs and documentation to be consistently lb-in or in-lb. This would require almost all torque procedures to be recalled and changed to have consistent units across all documentation and procedure. Even the generic guidance like 17-20MU-07 April 1 2018 has "10 in-oz to 2,000 lb-ft" in its Table 1 tolerance. For the sake of torque measurement, while they are not technically the same, we will treat them so for the context of NAVAIR. 

For short substitution, I would recomend to be consistent with what the procedure says which is in-lb. I don't think it matters in terms of technical which unit is used, but for the sake of auditing and quality, it would be better to stay consistent with what the procedure or SOP dicates SDB's Certificate of Calibration should be calibrated in.

This disprency in units most likely stems from legacy US torque wrench makers in the auto industry and similar fields. Back then, the standard was to us in-lb, but current ASTM and NIST recomendations are to use lb-in.

ProbDesc: The procedure of 17-20MU-97 (16 0ct 2024) focuses on the calibration of Himmelstein Torquemeter with model: 48002V1-3NFZ and 49802V25-1NFZ, cage: 27573. From the perspective of metrology standards and physical principles, the procedure describes the dead-weight method to calibrate Torquemeter using a standard lever arm and standard weights to create standard torques. Also using Power Supply to supply an excitation voltage of input of Strain Gauge and using a Digital Multimeter to measure voltage of output of Strain Gauge. A comprehensive metrological review of the NAVAIR 17-20MU-97 procedure reveals critical technical issues as follows: 1/ Traceability issue: The procedure uses a formula (Item B.3) based on End-Point linearization method to calculate the ideal output voltage with “maximum voltage capacity” and “maximum torque capacity” (as the example of item B.3 for the result of sensitivity factor 0.005 V/lb.in) is not traceability because these two parameters come from specifications of manufacturer, not track back to higher standard. Consequently, the reference baseline itself is theoretically untraceable. 2/ Linearization issue: The End-point linearization method of the procedure does not match ASTM E2428 – 22 (item 6.1.2 Curve fitting). ASTM determines the Least Square method to predict deflection of Strain Gauge throughout the verified range of Torque. The attached file of “Technical Calibration Issue 17-20MU-97” is the case study with the data on 01DEC 2025, Model: 48002V1-3NFZ, S/N: 48002V09160553, Certificate #: 65101-5335-247080. This case study represents the advantage factors of Least Square method compared to the End-point method. 3/ Tangent angle issue: The procedure lacks a leveling mechanism to adjust the tangent angle between the cable and the Lever Arm’s arc (AKO TSD125-S). This operational impact makes an alignment error introducing a high calibration risk. Request to review ICP 17-20MU-97 and to append the ASTM E2428 regression dataset to the device profile for the purpose of enhancing the reliability of calibrating Torquemeter.
TEInst:
Metrology Engineering at FRCSW has looked into the three items of concern regarding the ICP 17-20MU-97 and has determined the following:

1: The utilization of OEM specifications is not to be of concern as these specifications are what customers use to ensure that the specifications of their purchased items meet their workload requirements. Using our standards will ensure that the specifications set by the OEM are met thus ensuring traceability, no action is necessary regarding this matter.

2: The mentioned ASTM E1418-22 item 6.1.2 reference has validity, however Metrology Engineering at FRCSW does not have authority to make changes to the procedure, please submit an ISE ticket to look further into the matter as the current characterization being performed is based on an end point linearization and further analysis may require equation re-evaluation.

3: Torque arm standard specification sheet mentions special angle plates in order to keep moment arm level while performing calibrations. Ensure that the curved edge at the end of the torque arm lies tangent to that of the weight pan's wire, doing so will ensure that the torque arm is being used correctly thus negating any issues. If problem persists, please submit an ISE ticket looking further into the matter.
WorkNotes:
The  first section listed by the technician lists that the there is a traceability issue because the LCP uses parameters provided by the manufacturer. Based on how calibration procedures are set, customers explicitely buy their TIs based on manufacturer specifications. using our standards will ensure that the specifications set by the OEM are met and therefore this seems to be a non issue. 

There's validity to what is being stated by the technician in regards to the procedure not using the correct methodoogy for appropriately linearizing the TI, technical documents such as the E2428 - 22 Standard Practice for Calibration and Verrifiation of Elastic torque measurement standards, which state under section 6.1.2 that the torque deflection curve of elastic torque measurement standards require a fitted polynomial equation to account for the nonlinearity of deflections that are measured though the range of torques. Using the formula listed within the procedure leaves room for error as the formila explicitely sections off the expected output voltages linearly in accordance with expected torque inputs.

Finally, tangent angle issues are mentioned by the Technician, and looking into the torque arm specsheet, special angle plates are mentioned to keep the monent arm level while calibrating. these torque arm plates are not mentioned within the procedure, however a depiction of the calibration is shown, being it that his is an establised 17-20 procedure, the calibration can be performed if setup is properly adhered to.
